title: Each update fixes some breaks others
body:
The latest update left my iPhone 12 Pro Max unable to let me to change the cover image. The change cover page crashes just as the change cover page appears.

Previous review:
Just noticed that I, a paying Notion Plus subscriber can no longer use Notion AI.  Welp, I’m definitely not going to use Notion AI now that I have to upgrade and pay more than 4 times what I normally pay yearly.  And you can’t turn it off or even hide it!  Everyone knows AI is very flawed and yet these tech companies want to charge so much for it!  And anyone who uses Notion knows how flawed it is, which makes it all the more frustrating.  It’s got a truly great structure to it making it incredibly versatile, but it’s like a plane with small wings and no engines.  But hey, you can pay for a somewhat dim flight attendant.

OK, this is my previous review:

Just updated the app, sad to see image files load but then turn white and require me to scroll back up and then over the images to get them to show. Every time I load the page with images in it I have to scroll up and down again. The white screen may not seem like much but it’s annoying in dim light or when updating a journal in bed at night with the lights out. Been using Notion for 8 months now and am kind of surprised this hasn’t been fixed yet.

My original review: it really needs a few things—most importantly, encryption for us poor folks. It looks like you have to be an enterprise customer to get anything resembling actual privacy and it’s unclear what you get is encryption. We live in a time where our data is making people tons of money. I’d rather they not make money off of my notes and my used habits. Also, this needs the same notes graph/map/diagram thingy that a few Notion competitors have that allows you to visualize how all of your notes are related to each other. It is such a cool and helpful way to see the big picture on your projects! The third thing I think it needs is just a slightly better UI. It does a lot but it can be pretty challenging to navigate/find everything. I haven’t checked yet but I suspect that YouTube is the user’s friend along these lines. Otherwise, Notion is a fricken Swiss Army Knife app—you can literally keep a journal, a journal within a journal, a wiki, multiple wikis, I can’t even list all the templates this thing has. It’s really nuts how much you can do with Notion! I just wish it had encryption and the other couple things it’s competition has.

title: Ultimate flexibility. Some elbow grease requires.
body:
Notion in a word - flexible. 

Simplicity. Probably not. 

That’s not a criticism. That’s testament to how much you can do with it. 

A file manager is simple. Make some folders, store some files. Search them. Useful? Yes. Powerful? Not really. Flexible. No. 

It’s got a singular purpose. 

Notion is flexible and powerful. The trade off is knowing where to start. 

Notion can be a workflow tool. It can be a blog hosting platform. It can manage projects. Organise data for you and tag it. Be a research vault, holding articles, audio, imagery and video, all tailored and presented just the way you like it. Not a flat structure of files. No, think a rich webpage with links passing to other pages, embedded media. The works. 

And it’s not that hard to get any of it working. Notion does a lot to make this as easy as it can be. It’s all GUI driven. It’s impressive. 

Sure it has quirks. Could you get something this flexible to work without them? Probably not. 

You will struggle to find a product as feature rich. Its AI tooling isn’t just a gimmick either. It can truely help you manage and create content. 

Ask yourself - do you need this much in a tool? If you need a fantastic collaboration platform; a place to collect and organise your research project; a project management tool to help run your SMB; a way to effectively manage you local soccer club - notion could be your answer. 

If you just want somewhere to save your photos, or store some files, it’s overkill. 

Overall an excellent product in the right context.

title: Another Poor iPad Version
body:
It’s wild to me that the iPad version of this app is as poorly optimised as it is. After getting a nice big iPad to handle simple notes, journals, and other organisation, I sort of assumed Notion would’ve figured out a satisfying experience to mirror all the other instances. Maybe I had my expectations out of whack. It’d be one thing if it was just the iPhone app (still disappointing) but certain functions just straight up don’t work, and major ones no less, like simply moving sections around.

I want to love Notion, but it’s so disappointing to know that something so well suited to the purpose of Notion as the iPad (at least, in my opinion) clearly isn’t a priority.

But hey, at least their shareholders got another AI chat bot to peddle in meetings.

title: Finally found a system that works with my brain
body:
I’ve tried a lot of productivity and organization apps over the years, but Notion is the first one that actually feels flexible enough to grow with how I think instead of forcing me into someone else’s system.

I originally started using it for notes and organization, but it quickly became a place where I could connect ideas, workflows, AI concepts, healthcare operations, and long-term planning in a way that feels natural and visual.

What I appreciate most is that it works for both structured thinking and creative thinking at the same time. I can build detailed workflow maps one minute and brainstorm future ideas the next without switching platforms.

As someone working in healthcare operations and AI workflow design, I also love how adaptable it is for building living systems instead of static documents.

It genuinely helped me feel more organized, focused, and excited about my ideas again.

Not much of a business subscription if you can’t more people!!!! The other really really bad thing is app startup time. I open my phone for a morning meeting, go to notion to start AI notes and it just sits there… I’m on WiFi, and the app takes so long to load up it misses the first part of the meeting - often the MOST critical part!  These two things take the app from great to something I can’t rely on. And if I can’t rely on it, then I have to have something else that I can rely on. Really unfortunate. I do recognize that the iPhone SE has a smaller screen than most phones, and it’s possible that this is a dynamic layout issue that only happens on smaller screens. Even if that’s the case, losing the button for an AI prompt area that I can’t even use feels really bad.

The rest of the app and Notion features are working wonderfully.

title: Outstanding
body:
Notion is an exceptional productivity app that excels in every aspect of modern digital workspace management.

Usability: Notion is remarkably intuitive, with a seamless drag‑and‑drop interface and flexible page structure that makes organizing notes, tasks, and databases effortless. Even new users can quickly navigate and build workflows without a steep learning curve.

Performance: The app runs smoothly across devices, with lightning‑fast syncing between desktop, mobile, and web. Pages load quickly, and even large databases or complex dashboards maintain consistent responsiveness.

Design: Its minimalist, clean, and elegant design enhances focus without distractions. Subtle typography, spacing, and colour options let users create aesthetically pleasing layouts while maintaining clarity.

Features: Notion offers a powerful all‑in‑one toolkit: collaborative workspaces, relational databases, kanban boards, calendars, wikis, AI assistance, and extensive templates. The flexibility to customise every page for personal or team needs makes it stand out.

Value: With its robust free plan and versatile paid options, Notion delivers exceptional value for individuals, students, and businesses alike. It replaces multiple apps, effectively reducing costs and streamlining workflows.

Overall, Notion sets the standard for productivity and organisation, offering a versatile and beautifully designed platform that empowers users to work smarter and more creatively.
